bio: La Tarara is one of those restaurants where, having worked in renowned restaurants around Spain, its owners decided to return to their home region to start this highly personal project. Fronting a square in the centre of town, the restaurant boasts a pleasantly surprising contemporary feel along with a few unusual decorative details such as verses from La Tarara by Federico García Lorca (the children’s song from which it takes its name) adorning the walls. The cuisine here is an updated version of traditional Andalucian dishes, in which almost all the ingredients are sourced locally or from the province of Cádiz. Make sure you try its version of the Italian “payogiana” as well as the croissant of red tuna tartare. The tasting menu here is announced “by word of mouth”!...
